{"command": "create", "path": "/workspace/README.md", "file_text": "# PVLib Python

PVLib Python is a Python library for modeling photovoltaic systems. It provides a wide range of functionalities for simulating solar radiation, weather conditions, and power generation.

## Installation

To install PVLib Python, you can use pip:

```bash
pip install pvlib
```

## Usage

PVLib Python provides several modules for different aspects of solar energy modeling. Here are some basic examples:

### Solar Radiation

PVLib Python includes a module called `solarposition` which calculates the position of the sun at any given location and time.

```python
import pvlib.solarposition

# Define the location
location = {
    'latitude': 34.052235,
    'longitude': -118.243724,
    'elevation': 0,
}

# Calculate the solar position
times = ['2023-04-01T12:00:00', '2023-04-01T13:00:00']
solar_position = pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition(times, location)

print(solar_position)
```

### Weather Conditions

PVLib Python also includes a module called `weatherdata` which retrieves weather data from various sources.

```python
import pvlib.weatherdata

# Define the location
location = {
    'latitude': 34.052235,
    'longitude': -118.243724,
    'elevation': 0,
}

# Retrieve weather data
weather_data = pvlib.weatherdata.get_weather(location, times)

print(weather_data)
```

### Power Generation

PVLib Python provides a module called `powermodels` which models power generation based on various factors.

```python
import pvlib.powermodels

# Define the location
location = {
    'latitude': 34.052235,
    'longitude': -118.243724,
    'elevation': 0,
}

# Define the solar position
solar_position = pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition(times, location)

# Define the weather data
weather_data = pvlib.weatherdata.get_weather(location, times)

# Model power generation
power_generation = pvlib.powermodels.compute_power_generation(solar_position, weather_data)

print(power_generation)
```

## Documentation

For more information and documentation, please visit the official PVLib Python website: https://pypi.org/project/pvlib/

## Contributing

Contributions to PVLib Python are welcome! Please read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

## License

PVLib Python is licensed under the MIT License. See LICENSE for details."}
